title: Section 89 — Causing miscarriage without woman's consent

content.overview: BNS s. 89 — Causing miscarriage without woman's consent.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Causing miscarriage without woman's consent. BNS restatement of IPC 313. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 313. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 89 is the rule on “Causing miscarriage without woman's consent”. The section provides that whoever commits the offence under section 88 without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 89 exists so that “Causing miscarriage without woman's consent” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

learningObjectives: Master the aggravated offence of causing miscarriage without the woman's consent under BNS s. 89.
Recognize the severe sentencing tier: imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and fine.
Appreciate that quickening of the fetus is irrelevant when consent is absent.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 89 provides that whoever commits the offence under section 88 without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Violently or deceitfully terminating a woman's pregnancy against her will constitutes an egregious assault on bodily autonomy and fetal life, warranting life imprisonment.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 89 (corresponding to IPC s. 313).
Substantive act: Committing the offence under Section 88 without the consent of the woman.
Scope: Applies whether the woman is quick with child or not.
Punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused caused the woman to miscarry.
The act was committed WITHOUT the consent of the woman.
The act was not done in good faith to save the life of the woman.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 89 elevates causing miscarriage to an offence punishable with imprisonment for life when perpetrated without the woman's consent. The total absence of consent transforms the offence into a supreme violation of the mother's person and bodily sovereignty. Under Section 89, the stage of pregnancy does not alter the maximum penalty: whether the woman is in the earliest weeks of pregnancy or quick with child, committing non-consensual miscarriage attracts life imprisonment or up to ten years imprisonment plus fine. Common scenarios include covertly administering abortifacient drugs in food or drink, or physically assaulting a pregnant woman to force abortion.
examples: Teaching example (Spiking food with abortifacients): A husband and in-laws, unhappy with prenatal sex determination or desiring no children, secretly mix abortifacient chemical compounds into a woman's soup without her knowledge or consent, causing her to miscarry. They are liable under s. 89.

Teaching example (Forced surgical procedure): An estranged partner forces a pregnant woman into an unlicensed clinic and intimidates a quack doctor into performing an abortion while she protests. The partner is liable under s. 89.
distinctions: Section 89 vs Section 88: Section 88 applies when miscarriage is caused with consent (or generally), punishable with 3 to 7 years; Section 89 specifically punishes causing miscarriage WITHOUT consent with life imprisonment.
Section 89 vs Section 90: Section 89 penalizes non-consensual miscarriage; Section 90 penalizes cases where the act intended to cause miscarriage results in the death of the woman.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who slipped misoprostol tablets into his girlfriend's water bottle without her knowledge, causing severe cramping and expulsion of the embryo, is liable under s. 89.
Rule: Causing miscarriage without the woman's consent constitutes an offence under BNS s. 89 punishable with up to life imprisonment.
Application: The victim was pregnant, the accused acted intentionally, and consent was absent due to clandestine administration.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 89.

Stage of pregnancy is immaterial (quick or not quick).

Protects both female bodily autonomy and potential life.
